page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with one thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. For I/O and connectivity, the system includes 3,800 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 34 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput across multi-threaded applications. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-core Geekbench ratings, and Clang software compilation benchmarks. Memory performance is equally capable, registering top-tier cached read throughput exceeding 9,000 GB/sec and strong uncached large-block bandwidth exceeding 347 GB/sec read and 163 GB/sec write. In-memory data performance is particularly prominent, marked by top-tier results in Redis SET throughput reaching 181.85 million operations per second and PassMark database operations, while static web serving throughput reaches 177.9 GB/sec.

Without hardware GPU acceleration, the platform is not designed for heavy artificial intelligence model generation or large-scale machine learning training, with LLM token processing falling into the average category. However, the combination of dedicated 64-core ARM compute density, balanced system memory, and 3.8 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage delivers high operational efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads. The instance is well matched for distributed key-value caches, transactional database clusters, CI/CD build pipelines, and high-concurrency web serving infrastructure.

Configured with 256 GB of system RAM, it maintains a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation alongside 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 34 Gbps baseline networking. Benchmark testing shows top-tier multi-threaded compute, software compilation, and in-memory transactional processing, highlighted by Redis SET throughput reaching 181.85 million operations per second and top-tier database operations. While lacking hardware GPU acceleration for large-scale AI training, its dense single-thread-per-core layout and direct-attached NVMe storage provide high throughput efficiency for enterprise databases, distributed key-value caches, large CI/CD build environments, and static web serving workloads.
